<a id="decomposition-of-the-continuation-condition--延续条件的分解"></a>
# Decomposition of the continuation condition

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`continuation-condition-decomposition` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F07 · [record](continuation-condition-decomposition.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Where the whole is admissible, the continuation condition is exactly the presupposition sub-true and boundary-invariant at every standpoint. Invariance is the conditional from presupposition to condition, carrying all it adds; with presupposition and covering everywhere, it is standpoint neutrality.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A claim about a self is super-true when it holds however the self's boundary is drawn among the admissible regions, sub-true when it holds as drawn at some admissible region, and boundary-invariant when, holding as drawn at one admissible region, it holds as drawn at every other. The presupposition at standpoint p, for a region: from p, the continuation of everything within it has significance at every step. (`Becoming.Boundary`, `Becoming.SuperTrue`, `Becoming.SubTrue`, `Becoming.BoundaryInvariant`, `Becoming.SignificantWithin`)
2. Wherever the whole is admissible, the presupposition at p is boundary-invariant exactly when, holding as the boundary is drawn anywhere, it holds as drawn at the whole; that is exactly the conditional from the presupposition to the continuation condition at p, with no presupposition assumed. There, where some continuation lacks significance from p, an invariant presupposition holds at no drawing: the step runs both ways. (`Becoming.boundaryInvariant_iff_extends`, `Becoming.boundaryInvariant_iff_conditional`, `Becoming.not_subTrue_of_invariant`)
3. Wherever the whole is admissible and the presupposition at p is sub-true, invariance is exactly the continuation condition at p: from p, the continuation of everything has significance at every step. The continuation condition being boundary neutrality for the significance of continuation, at one standpoint the step is boundary neutrality. (`Becoming.boundaryInvariant_iff_all`, `Becoming.Unrestricted`)
4. Let every formation lie within some admissible boundary of every self (covering), let each standpoint's presupposition be sub-true, and let it be boundary-invariant: then the continuation condition holds. (`Becoming.unrestricted_of_presupposed`)
5. Where the whole is admissible for every self, the continuation condition is exactly the presupposition sub-true and invariant at every standpoint; so along any relation, a self's boundaries being the regions that hold its center and are closed under it. Where each center's closure is the whole, the whole is the only boundary, invariance holds trivially, and the continuation condition is exactly the presupposition sub-true at every standpoint. (`Becoming.unrestricted_iff_presupposed`, `Becoming.unrestricted_iff_presupposed_along`, `Becoming.unrestricted_iff_presupposed_of_whole`, `Becoming.Boundary.only_whole`)
6. Corollaries, with the whole admissible for every self and the presupposition sub-true and invariant at every standpoint: standpoints retain alike, and living significance holds at the level of claims on every reading in which a claim's significance is that of some formation's continuation at some step. (`Becoming.retains_agree_of_presupposed`, `Becoming.Web.retains_agree`, `Becoming.Valuation.significant_of_presupposed`, `Becoming.Valuation.premises_of_unrestricted`)
7. Significance is standpoint-invariant when what has significance from one standpoint has it from every other, the rule of standpoint neutrality. Along a relation, with every formation within some center's closure and every standpoint's presupposition sub-true, it gives the continuation condition and is equivalent to boundary-invariance at every standpoint. Without the presupposition at every standpoint the two come apart. (`Becoming.StandpointInvariant`, `Becoming.unrestricted_of_standpointInvariant`, `Becoming.boundaryInvariant_iff_standpointInvariant`, `Becoming.OneCounts.forms_apart`, `Becoming.OneCounts.sig`)
8. So the premises carry to the significance of continuation two decompositions already in the core: living significance as a seed, relational and standpoint neutrality on a connected whole with some living claim, and, where every living claim is some standpoint's own, living significance as self-significance at every standpoint with standpoint neutrality. (`Becoming.Valuation.significant_iff`, `Becoming.Valuation.significant_iff_held`)
9. Where each center's system is the whole, the continuation condition is exactly the presupposition sub-true along sharing a condition at every standpoint; one common condition, in which every formation takes part, suffices. Clearing is one system, so there the continuation condition is exactly that presupposition at every standpoint. (`Becoming.Flow.unrestricted_iff_system_presupposed`, `Becoming.Flow.unrestricted_iff_presupposed_of_common`, `Becoming.Flow.system_whole_of_common`, `Becoming.Clearing.system_presupposition`, `Becoming.Clearing.system_whole`)
10. In Clearing, with nothing significant, the presupposition is invariant at every standpoint and the whole a boundary of every self, while the continuation condition fails. With significance bounded by each feeding closure, every presupposition is sub-true and the whole a boundary, while the continuation condition fails: the clearer's presupposition is not invariant, and significance is not standpoint-invariant. (`Becoming.Clearing.without_presupposition`, `Becoming.Clearing.without_invariance`, `Becoming.Clearing.without_standpoint_invariance`, `Becoming.bounded`, `Becoming.WithinClosure`)
11. Were each self's only admissible boundary its feeding closure, the same significance would make every presupposition sub-true and invariant, the dweller would lie within no admissible boundary of the clearer, and the continuation condition would still fail. (`Becoming.Clearing.with_fixed_boundary`, `Becoming.Clearing.dweller_beyond`, `Becoming.Flow.WithinFeeding`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Covering (every formation within some admissible boundary of every self), the presupposition sub-true at every standpoint, and boundary-invariance are hypotheses, not Lean axioms; along a relation the admissible boundaries are every region holding the center that is closed under the relation, the whole included, and that admissibility is a substantive choice.
- Discrete steps, counted from step 0; natural-number levels, needs and amounts.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The decomposition locates the step and does not lower the continuation condition: invariance is the conditional from the presupposition to the continuation condition, and given the presupposition it is the continuation condition at that standpoint; logically, A ⇔ P ∧ (P → A) given A → P. Witness: `Becoming.boundaryInvariant_iff_conditional`.
- The presupposition, covering and invariance are hypotheses of the theorems, which give no derivation of them.
- It does not compel the step: one who denies it can hold the presupposition only relative to a drawing or a standpoint, or give it up. Witness: `Becoming.Clearing.without_invariance`.
- Which premise each rival denies (operational closure, a vague self, a graded weight falling to zero, a present-aim evaluator) is located, not refuted; the literature is from prior knowledge.
- The step from significance to a reason, to motivation or to practice lies outside the theorems.
- **Counterexample:** Each premise is needed: Clearing.without_presupposition, without_invariance, without_standpoint_invariance and with_fixed_boundary each drop a premise or change the admissible class, and the continuation condition fails; without the presupposition everywhere the two forms of invariance come apart (OneCounts.forms_apart). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Boundaries.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A conditional law does not make its antecedent universal; a theorem's premise is not thereby necessary for every achievement.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

In “Truth exist” Ren wrote: “There is a set of universal invariations, that for every universe, becoming happens, the law follows”; “There is no absolute self, and the continuation goes beyond one’s cycle of life, goes beyond one’s death.” Earlier Ren wrote that the self is “a cognitive model which can not justify itself without some sort of "belief"”, and that “we” are “the universe/ecosystem that realizes its own existence”. The AI proposed that the axiom may follow from three claims it read from Ren's words, one step short (in the source); on review, the result is a decomposition of the axiom, not a reduction. The author's reading (an AI argument, adopted on Ren's delegation, DELEGATED-CHOICES D21; the step of invariance stays open as a question of warrant, chapter sections 6.5 and 8.5, not as one pending Ren, D45): the presupposition reads the “belief” without which, Ren wrote, the self cannot justify itself, and using it as a premise is the AI's step; along a relation covering holds by construction, Ren's “we” supports the whole as one drawing, and “There is no absolute self” does not by itself give covering; “for all beings” reads most directly as standpoint-invariance, the rule of N_std, and extending “universal invariations” to significance is the AI's reading; Ren's levels read as three readings of the presupposition: super-true, sub-true along affecting, and sub-true along the empty relation. Super-truth and sub-truth are named from supervaluation (Fine 1975) and subvaluation (Hyde 1997), from prior knowledge; the other names are the AI's. G0 itself is no longer an axiom: Ren folded it after the audit of its uses came out clean.
